purpose: First execution of ODB structure verification, result_ref round-trip and mtime semantics review against a REAL Abaqus-produced ODB (leftovers P1-LEFTOVER-02, P1-LEFTOVER-04, P2-LEFTOVER-02, P2-LEFTOVER-03).
not_proven_by_this_file: watchdog behaviour on large implicit solves (P1-LEFTOVER-01) - this is a single-element static job
real-scale cache restore timing (P2-LEFTOVER-03) - payload is 2 extractions, 8 KB

sample.why_not_committed: .gitignore:28 ignores *.odb; only the description below can be committed

positive_case.note: First time the odbAccess.openOdb() path ran against a real ODB

negative_cases.error_excerpt: Cannot open file ... ***ERROR: The Abaqus database

b2_structure_verification.conclusion: Layered defence holds on real data: the pre-filter rejects size/fill/plaintext classes; truncation and header corruption pass the pre-filter but are caught by odbAccess.openOdb. The pre-filter alone is insufficient, which was already documented; this run confirms both layers are load-bearing.
b2_structure_verification.why_still_open: Positive and negative evidence now exists on a real ODB, but on a single-element static job. No large implicit ODB has been verified. Closing P1-LEFTOVER-02 needs a real ODB from case_07_jounce_bumper or equivalent.

b3_result_ref_roundtrip.conclusion: Cold extract -> cache write -> cache hit -> disk restore all hold on a real ODB with real odbAccess data. The round-trip is confirmed end to end.
b3_result_ref_roundtrip.why_still_open: Same ODB, 2 extractions. A production-scale extraction (many requirements, large meshes) is not covered.

p2_leftover_03_restore_timing.why_still_open: The payload is 8 KB / 2 extractions. The <10ms budget has now been met on real ODB output, but not at real engineering scale. This does not close the leftover, which is explicitly about scale.

b4_mtime_semantics_review.question: Does 'ODB mtime must be later than .sta' actually discriminate corrupt from valid ODBs?

finding_1_valid_odb_would_be_rejected.case: byte-identical copy of the VALID ODB, mtime set to 09:00:00 (earlier than .sta at 09:28:00)
finding_1_valid_odb_would_be_rejected.meaning: A legitimate, fully readable ODB is rejected purely by timestamp ordering. This is a false rejection on real data, not a hypothetical.

finding_2_rule_cannot_catch_corruption.meaning: Both corrupted files satisfy the proposed mtime rule. The rule has zero discriminating power for the corruption classes it was meant to catch.

b4_mtime_semantics_review.conclusion: The mtime comparison is refuted in both directions on real data: it rejects a valid file and accepts corrupt ones. It must not be implemented as a recovery gate.
b4_mtime_semantics_review.recommendation: Revise the contract text rather than implement the rule. Recommended replacement criterion, which this run shows IS discriminating: reject if the file is smaller than 1024 bytes, uniform-fill, or plaintext; then require odbAccess.openOdb() to open it and yield at least one non-initial step with at least one frame. mtime carries no additional signal.
b4_mtime_semantics_review.why_still_open: The governance plan still contains the mtime requirement. Revising contract text requires an explicit decision; this evidence supports revision but does not itself amend the plan.

reproduction.extraction_requires: a customer project root OUTSIDE the repo with input/, working/, solver/, evidence/, delivery/ (paths.require_customer_project_context)
reproduction.note: The cold extraction call fails with a production guard if the ODB lives inside the repository. Place the ODB under an external project root before extracting.
